newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES FIRMER AS LIQUIDITY FALLS.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES FIRMER AS LIQUIDITY FALLS.

text.p: The level of liquidity on Zimbabwe's money market came off on Monday with short-term trading rates firmer compared to Friday's levels, dealers said.

"It looks like the market is becoming a bit short -- this week we are expecting maturities only on Tuesday. Also banks are making state reserve adjustment payments to the central bank and that will take money off the system," a dealer commented.
He said discount houses were on Monday taking up 91-day central bank bills at 20.21 percent and selling them into the market at 20 percent, up from Friday's 19.50 percent.

NCD bills redeemable after 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought and sold firmer at 22.75 and 20.25 percent respectively from 22 and 20 percent while bankers acceptances were buying at a steady 20.5 percent but selling at 20 percent, up from 19.50 percent.
Call money was however quoted half a percentage point easier at 19.50 percent.
The central Reserve Bank put Monday's start-off position at a Z$70 million surplus, down from Friday's Z$342 million.
